item.title: Artificial Intelligence Could Help Prevent Sexual Assault In Prisons
item.description:
# Artificial Intelligence Could Help Prevent Sexual Assault In Prisons This voice experience is generated by AI.
This voice experience is generated by AI.
## Summary AI platforms, like Verus Vision AI, can analyze live video feeds to detect emerging risks such as assaults or self-harm indicators in real-time, enabling proactive intervention rather than post-incident review.
## Moving from Recording History to Preventing Harm One company attempting to apply this approach is [LEO Technologies](https://leotechnologies.com/), which recently introduced [Verus Vision AI](https://leotechnologies.com/verus-vision-ai/), an artificial intelligence solution designed specifically for correctional environments. According to the company, the software application transforms existing correctional camera systems into an active operational intelligence network capable of continuously analyzing live video feeds and identifying emerging risks.
Steven Harpe, LEO’s Chief Product and Technology Officer and former Executive Director of the Oklahoma Department of Corrections told me in an interview, "Verus Vision AI transforms existing camera infrastructure into an active layer of operational intelligence, agencies can recognize developing threats sooner, preserve objective evidence, and maximize the effectiveness of limited staff.
## Strengthening Investigations Through Objective Evidence An AI platform capable of automatically identifying individuals present, preserving relevant video, reconstructing timelines and correlating movement patterns could significantly reduce investigative time while improving accuracy.
## Future of PREA Artificial intelligence, sophisticated video analytics and operational intelligence platforms offer correctional leaders capabilities that lawmakers could scarcely have imagined when PREA became law.

item.title: Frugal AI: the key to embedding artificial intelligence in combat optronics
item.description:
# Frugal AI: the key to embedding artificial intelligence in combat optronics Deep learning techniques now meet a clear operational need, and frugal AI – artificial intelligence that achieves strong performance while using minimal resources – is a potential game-changer for armed forces in a battlespace of unprecedented complexity and uncertainty. Building on Thales's know-how in this strategic area, the first deep learning AI of its kind will soon equip the TALIOS optronic pod for combat aircraft, charting new territory in the race for real-time target detection and classification
## Embedding AI in the systems deployed by combat aircraft and other high-tech platforms is anything but a passing fad In this context, artificial intelligence is the third eye, the bridge to heightened awareness and deeper insight, and the key to operational superiority.
The TALIOS targeting pod in service since 2021 is a fine illustration of Thales's expertise in deep learning technologies, with a brand new deep learning module known as ATD/R (Automatic Target Detection and Recognition) currently undergoing live flight tests.
